better_overall.reason: B should be published: it is the more polished page with larger type, its flow suits seventy-year-olds best (a review step before confirming, a clear success page saying what happens next, family members allowed to share one phone, plus a roster page for staff), and its weak spots are text fixes in config.js, whereas A, though more distinctive and more careful about facts, overwrites the first sign-up when a second person uses the same phone for the same class, which is common for elderly couples or a child registering both parents.

post_code_notes: The code makes A look more distinctive than the screenshots showed. Choosing a class draws a red, hand-drawn circle around the 楷/行 character in its 米字格, like a teacher's mark, and the confirmation page reuses it. The blank area next to an unselected class name is kept free for the '已选' label, so it is deliberate, but it still looks empty before a choice is made. A's different input widths on desktop (20rem and 16rem) are a deliberate choice to match expected content length, not a bug. A's text is larger than I estimated: 20px body, 24px labels and inputs, 64px controls. B uses 20px body, 24-27px labels, inputs and class names, and 64-70px controls. Neither page loads a web font. Both rely on a locally installed Kaiti font, so on many phones (most Android models, possibly iOS) B's brush-style title and A's specimen characters fall back to a serif or sans face. The macOS screenshots are therefore the best case. This weakens B's visual lead more than A's, because A's grid is drawn in SVG, but I would still keep more_beautiful = B. Flows: A submits from one page. It shows a GOV.UK-style error summary plus inline errors, a busy state and timeout, and network or server messages that reassure 'your entries are still here'. After a successful submit, A's confirmation page suggests taking a screenshot and offers an edit button that replaces the entry. B goes form, then review (with a compact header so 确认报名 is visible without scrolling), then success, duplicate or switch result. It handles the Android back button and updates inline errors as the user types ('您填了 10 位'). Data: A identifies a sign-up by phone + class. A couple sharing a phone, or a child signing up both parents, therefore loses the first registration, and only the second person is told. B identifies a sign-up by name + phone and offers '再帮别人报名'. But a person who wants to change class is told '请联系老师', and no contact appears unless config.js is filled in. B also adds a password-protected roster with tap-to-call and a CSV download. A only writes a CSV on the server disk. Honesty: A openly says that location, start date and payment will be sent later to the phone number. B states invented process promises as fact ('老师会打这个电话联系您', '我们会尽快打电话和您确认'), along with invented curriculum details ('从握笔和基本笔画学起', a 楷书 prerequisite). These are editable in config.js. Location and contact are hidden when empty rather than invented.
